pr_title: feat(medusa): Allow regexp in CORS configuration

comments.body: `new RegExp(m[2], m[3])` keeps the `g` and `y` flags, and the `[gimsuy]*` pattern and the spec (`/ab#/[c]/ig`) explicitly allow them. The `cors` middleware checks regexp origins with `origin.test(...)`. A `g` or `y` regexp keeps `lastIndex` between calls. Take `/https:\/\/.*\.example\.com/g` in `store_cors`. The first request from an allowed origin passes. The next test starts at the old `lastIndex` and fails, so the middleware returns no CORS headers and the browser rejects the request, which then alternates. Drop `g` and `y` from the flags, or don't accept them.

`str.split(",")` runs before regexp detection, so a regexp that contains a comma gets split into pieces. An example is `/^https:\/\/a{1,3}\.example\.com$/`, with the quantifier `{1,3}`. The pieces `/^https:\/\/a{1` and `3}\.example\.com$/` each fail `buildRegexpIfValid` and fall back to plain strings. The intended origin never matches and no error is raised. Split on commas outside a delimited regexp, or document that commas are unsupported.
